question: The SLUDGE features of organophosphorus poisoning — salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, gastrointestinal cramps, and emesis — are caused by excess acetylcholine acting at muscarinic receptors.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. SLUDGE features arise from excess acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors following acetylcholinesterase inhibition. Atropine, a competitive muscarinic antagonist, reverses these secretory and smooth-muscle effects. The nicotinic features (muscle fasciculations, weakness, paralysis) are addressed by pralidoxime.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. SLUDGE is the muscarinic component of the cholinergic toxidrome. Organophosphorus compounds inhibit acetylcholinesterase, leading to acetylcholine accumulation at both muscarinic (secretory glands, smooth muscle) and nicotinic (skeletal muscle, autonomic ganglia) synapses. SLUDGE features are muscarinic and respond to atropine.
